messages.subject: GPS and VHF (outliers, models HR, residency)
parts:
Hey there,
I'm pretty new to working with animal movement and telemetry data.

I have data from 14 individuals, some of them are marked with GPS, others with VHF and some with both during all the marked period.

I wanted to asked if the individuals that have both (GPS and VHF), do I have to separate both periods and analyze them separately (outliers and HR with AKDE)  or because there are models to account for irregular schedules, etc would be okey to use all data at once?

Also, I think I have some individuals that aren't residential. I saw on some of you videos that you check that by coloring the positions by time. That would be enoguh to separate residency periods and calculate several HR? I also read something about Net square displacement...


Thank you so much,
E

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: GPS and VHF (outliers, models HR, residency)
parts:
Hi Elennaa,

Irregular sampling is fine with continuous-time models. If the sampled movements are small relative to the location errors, you might need to calibrate the GPS and VHF data separately before you merge them with tbind().

The stability of the variogram is also a good signature of residency.

Occasional excursions can be okay, if there is enough data to support that. The variograms and effective sample sizes will tell you.

Best,
Chris
